content.content:
# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.
# Acceptance criteria

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 3, 6 · Agent: read-only

This list is an input, the same in every run of this project: the agent does not derive, add, merge or reword criteria. Each criterion states one observable behaviour (Given / When / Then) and cites its story and rules. "Rejected" always means: the API answers with an error status and field errors, no database row and no JSON copy are created, and no email is sent. The open questions are answered in `scope.md` (OQ-01 to OQ-06).

Common terms used below:

- *valid external submission*: registration type `EXTERNAL`; first name, last name, email, organization filled; every mandatory consent given; a reCAPTCHA token the verifier accepts; zero or more distinct active option ids available to the type.
- *valid student submission*: as above with type `STUDENT` and study institution, study programme and student ID instead of organization.

## US-001 External participant registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-001-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid external submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-001-02 | Given the external form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, organization) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-001-03 | Given a valid external submission whose text fields have leading and trailing spaces, when it is accepted, then the stored values have the spaces removed. | BR-02 |
| AC-001-04 | Given the external form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-001-05 | Given the external form, when an option id is unknown, inactive or listed twice, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, SR-04, OQ-04 |
| AC-001-06 | Given the external form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-001-07 | Given the external form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01, scope (anti-automation) |
| AC-001-08 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "external participant", then the page shows exactly the external fields, the active options grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities, and every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05 |

## US-002 Student registration

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-002-01 | Given active options are configured, when a valid student submission is sent, then it is accepted (HTTP 201) and the response contains the new registration id. | BR-01, BR-04 |
| AC-002-02 | Given the student form, when any one required field (first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID) is missing, empty or only whitespace, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that field. | BR-01, BR-02 |
| AC-002-03 | Given the student form, when the email does not have a valid email format, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the email field. | BR-03 |
| AC-002-04 | Given an active option configured as not available to students, when a student submission selects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for the options. | BR-04, OQ-01 |
| AC-002-05 | Given the student form, when a mandatory consent is not given, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) with an error for that consent. | BR-05, OQ-02 |
| AC-002-06 | Given the student form, when the reCAPTCHA token is missing or the verifier rejects it, then the submission is rejected (HTTP 400) and nothing is stored. | SR-01 |
| AC-002-07 | Given the registration page, when the participant chooses "student", then the page shows exactly the student fields and only the active options available to students, grouped by category, with every consent checkbox unchecked. | BR-01, BR-04, BR-05, OQ-01 |

## US-003 Configurable conference options

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-003-01 | Given a configuration with active and inactive options, when the form configuration is requested, then it lists only the active options, each with its identifier, display name, category and the registration types it is available to. | BR-04 |
| AC-003-02 | Given the backend is started with a different options configuration (an option added, one deactivated), when the form configuration is requested, then it reflects the new configuration, with no code change. | AR-04 |
| AC-003-03 | Given an options configuration that is invalid (duplicate identifier, unknown category, missing name), when the backend starts, then it refuses to start. | AR-04 |

## US-004 Registration confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-004-01 | Given a filled form, when the backend accepts the registration, then the page shows a confirmation with the participant's name and the selected options, and the form is no longer shown. | BR-06 |
| AC-004-02 | Given a filled form, when the backend rejects the registration with field errors, then no confirmation is shown, each error is shown next to its field, and the entered values remain. | BR-06, NFR-03 |
| AC-004-03 | Given a form with an empty required field or an invalid email, when the participant submits, then the page shows the field errors and sends no request to the backend. | NFR-03 |
| AC-004-04 | Given a filled form, when the backend fails or cannot be reached, then no confirmation is shown and a general error message without technical details is shown. | BR-06, SB-07 |

## US-005 Reliable registration storage

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-005-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then the database holds one registration with the type, every submitted field, the selected options, each consent with the time it was given, and the time of registration. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-02 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then a JSON copy named after the registration id exists in the JSON copy directory and contains the registration as accepted. | BR-07 |
| AC-005-03 | Given the JSON copy cannot be written, when a valid submission is sent, then the API answers with an error (not 201) and no registration is left in the database. | BR-07, AR-05 |
| AC-005-04 | Given a valid submission with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž, Č, Š, Ž) in the names and institution, when it is accepted, then the database row and the JSON copy contain the text unchanged. | BR-03, NFR-01 |

## US-006 Participant email confirmation

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-006-01 | Given a valid submission, when it is accepted, then one email is sent to the participant's address naming the conference, the participant and the selected options. | US-006 |
| AC-006-02 | Given a submission whose text fields contain line breaks, header-like text or HTML markup, when the confirmation email is sent, then the email has no additional headers or recipients and the markup appears only as literal text. | SR-05 |
| AC-006-03 | Given the mail server is unavailable, when a valid submission is sent, then the registration is still accepted (HTTP 201) and stored. | OQ-03, OQ-03 |

## US-007 Organizer notification

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-007-01 | Given organizer addresses are configured, when a registration is accepted, then each organizer address receives a notification email containing the submitted registration data. | US-007 |
| AC-007-02 | Given a registration is accepted, when the organizer notification is sent, then it has a JSON attachment whose content equals the stored JSON copy. | US-007, BR-07, SR-07 |

## US-008 Registration export

| ID | Criterion | Refs |
|---|---|---|
| AC-008-01 | Given stored registrations, when an organizer requests the export with valid organizer credentials, then the response is an Excel workbook (`.xlsx`) with one row per registration, containing its type, fields, selected options, consents and registration time. | BR-08 |
| AC-008-02 | Given stored registrations, when the export is requested without credentials or with wrong credentials, then it is refused (HTTP 401) and no registration data is returned. | BR-08, SB-02 |
| AC-008-03 | Given a registration with Slovenian characters, when the organizer exports, then the workbook cell contains the text unchanged. | NFR-01 |
| AC-008-04 | Given organizer HTTPS-only access is on, when the export is requested with valid credentials over plain HTTP from a client that is not on localhost, then it is refused and no registration data is returned. | SR-06 |

## Traceability

| Story | Criteria |
|---|---|
| US-001 | AC-001-01 … AC-001-08 |

# Business rules

> Owner: Product owner · Read in: phases 1, 6 · Agent: read-only

## Rules

| ID | Rule |
|---|---|
| BR-01 | There are two registration types: external participant and student. Each has the fixed fields listed under Data; configuration never changes them. |
| BR-02 | Required fields are never empty; leading and trailing whitespace is not significant. |
| BR-03 | Email has a valid email format. Text accepts Unicode, including Slovenian characters (č, š, ž). |
| BR-04 | Options are grouped as workshops, events, meals and other activities. Only active options can be selected; unknown or inactive options are rejected. |
| BR-05 | Mandatory consents must be given and are never preselected. |
| BR-06 | The in-application confirmation is shown only after the registration was accepted. |
| BR-07 | An accepted registration is stored in the database and as a raw JSON copy on persistent storage. |
| BR-08 | Only organizers can obtain the registration list; it is not reachable without organizer access. |

## Data

| Form or entity | Fields (all required) |
|---|---|
| External participant | first name, last name, email, organization / institution |
| Student | first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme, student ID |
| Conference option | stable identifier, display name, category (workshop, event, meal, other), active or inactive |
| Consent | which consents exist and their wording: `OQ-02` |

## Glossary

- Participant: a person who registers, external or student.
- Organizer: conference staff who receive notifications and export registrations.
- Option: a selectable workshop, event, meal or other activity.
- Active option: an option currently offered for selection.
- Raw JSON copy: the registration exactly as accepted, stored as a file for backup.

# Security requirements

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/security/security-baseline.md` (SB-01 … SB-14); do not repeat those here.

## Verification standard

| Component | Standard | Level | Reason if above the default |
|---|---|---|---|
| backend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |
| frontend | OWASP ASVS 5.0 | Level 1 | |

Level 1 is a deliberate choice: the only authentication is one organizer role for one export operation, and the personal data is contact and study data, not sensitive data. Where a requirement below is more specific than ASVS, it applies as well.

## Authentication and authorization

- Participants are anonymous; there are no participant accounts.
- One organizer role may export registrations (BR-08). The mechanism is decided in phase 2, using the organizer credentials from `secrets.env.example`; identity providers are out of scope.
- Everything else (options, registration) is public but protected by SR-01 and SR-03.

## Personal data

| Data item | Purpose | Retention | Shown/exported to |
|---|---|---|---|
| First and last name | identify the participant | `OQ-06` | organizers (email, export) |
| Email | confirmation and contact | `OQ-06` | participant, organizers |
| Organization / institution | attendance records | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Study institution, programme, student ID | student registration | `OQ-06` | organizers |
| Selected options | plan workshops, events and meals | `OQ-06` | participant (confirmation), organizers |
| Consents given, with timestamp | proof of consent (SB-14) | `OQ-06` | organizers |

## Project requirements

| ID | Requirement |
|---|---|
| SR-01 | Every registration is protected by Google reCAPTCHA v2 and verified on the backend; the frontend check alone is never enough. |
| SR-02 | reCAPTCHA test mode is enabled only by environment configuration, never by default; production refuses to start with test mode on or with empty keys. |
| SR-03 | Every public `/api` endpoint (form configuration, registration, export) is rate limited per client, and request bodies have a size limit. |
| SR-04 | Option identifiers are checked against the active configured set (BR-04). |
| SR-05 | Email content is generated safely: user input cannot inject headers or markup. |
| SR-06 | Organizer credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP, except on localhost. |
| SR-07 | The export and the organizer email expose only registration data, never internal fields or other system data. |
| SR-08 | The reverse proxy in front of the backend never forwards a client-supplied `Host` header; it sets the upstream host itself. |

## Overrides

None.
# Quality requirements

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: phases 2, 6, 7 · Agent: read-only

Adds to `general/quality/` (definition of done, test strategy, severity scale); do not repeat those here.

## Non-functional requirements

| ID | Category (performance, availability, accessibility, localisation, usability, …) | Requirement | How it is checked |
|---|---|---|---|
| NFR-01 | Localisation | Names and other text with Slovenian characters (č, š, ž) survive the form, database, JSON copy, emails and Excel export unchanged. | an end-to-end test with such input |
| NFR-02 | Reliability | Stored registrations and JSON copies survive recreation of every container. | runtime demonstration: `docker compose down` then `up`, data still present |
| NFR-03 | Usability | The frontend validates fields before submission and shows the backend's field errors next to the fields. | component tests |
| NFR-04 | Availability | The backend reports health and readiness, and the containers use them in health checks. | runtime demonstration |

## Thresholds

These thresholds are the **quality gate** of the project: the same in every run, per component (backend, frontend), over the scope and with the tests defined in `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`. The agent works until each component meets them, then stops adding tests for that component (rules and stop rule: "Quality gate" in `measurement-scope.md`). The rows below are read by `tools/build-report.mjs`; keep the format `>= <number> %`.

| Measure | Threshold |
|---|---|
| Line coverage (all levels together) | >= 95 % |
| Mutation score (adjusted) | >= 90 % |
| Branch coverage | record only |

## Mutation scope

The paths or packages whose code is mutated, the same in every run of this project (default: all production code of the component). Selection rule: validation, security, persistence and business-rule code. Rules: `general/quality/measurement-scope.md`.

| Component | Paths or packages | Exclusions and reason |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `si.konferenca.registration.**` (all production code under the root package, including validation, security, persistence, business-rule, mail and export code) | The `@SpringBootApplication` entry-point class (no logic); generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |
| frontend | `src/**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,vue}` (all production source of the frontend) | Test files, type-declaration files (`*.d.ts`), the bootstrap file that only mounts the app, generated code. Nothing else may be excluded. |

The scope is all production code of both components, so mutation scores are on the same basis in every run. It is the root package and the source folder, not a list of sub-packages, because the agent chooses the sub-packages in phase 2. Each component's full automated suite runs against it (`measurement-scope.md`, "Mutation score").

## Additional done criteria

| ID | Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| DoD-P01 | Against the running local stack: one external and one student registration succeed. | runtime demonstration log |
| DoD-P02 | Each registration is in PostgreSQL and has its JSON copy. | database query, file listing |
| DoD-P03 | The participant email and the organizer email (with the JSON attachment) arrive in Mailpit. | Mailpit API output |
| DoD-P04 | The organizer downloads a valid Excel workbook; the same request without organizer access is refused. | response codes, opened workbook |
| DoD-P05 | The production reCAPTCHA code path is tested against a mocked verification endpoint, including a rejected token. | test report |

## Overrides

None.

| # | Finding | Handling |
|---|---|---|
| G-01 | OQ-01 says an option not available to the registration type is rejected for both types, but only the student case has a criterion (AC-002-04). | No conflict: the specification applies OQ-01 to both types; tests follow the criteria list. |
| G-02 | AC-006-03 cites `OQ-03` twice in its Refs. | Typo with no behavioural effect; no decision. |
| G-03 | AC-008-04 says the export over plain HTTP from a non-localhost client is "refused" but gives no status or whether to redirect. | D-11 (non-blocking, pending review). |
| G-04 | E2E-01 needs at least one active option per category and E2E-02 needs options not shown to students, but the inputs give no shipped options configuration (only the consent, OQ-02). | D-12 (non-blocking, pending review). |
| G-05 | The language of the form, confirmation and emails is not stated; the only given wording (OQ-02 consent) is English. | D-13 (non-blocking, pending review). |
| G-06 | No maximum length is given for any text field, yet SR-03 requires a body size limit and the database needs column sizes. | D-14 (non-blocking, pending review). |
| G-07 | The status for AC-005-03 ("an error, not 201") and the field key of the reCAPTCHA error (AC-001-07, AC-002-06) are not given. | Not visible to a user beyond AC-004-04's general message; fixed in the specification and contracts, no decision. |
EOF

## D-11: Response to organizer credentials over plain HTTP (AC-008-04, SR-06)
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: AC-008-04 requires refusal but does not say how; SR-06 says credentials are never accepted over plain HTTP except on localhost.
- Options: 1. (chosen, conservative) Answer HTTP 403 with a general error and no data, without evaluating the credentials and without a redirect; 2. Redirect (308) to HTTPS, which invites clients to resend the credentials.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review

## D-12: Shipped conference options configuration
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: G-04 in \`docs/01_requirements-check.md\`; the inputs define the option fields (BR-04, OQ-01) but no shipped option set, while E2E-01 and E2E-02 depend on one.
- Options: 1. (chosen) Ship an example configuration with at least one active option per category available to both types, at least one active option available only to external participants, and one inactive option; the operator replaces it through configuration (AR-04); 2. Ship an empty option set.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review

## D-13: User-facing language
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: G-05; no language is stated for the form, confirmation, errors or emails. The only given wording, the OQ-02 consent text, is English.
- Options: 1. (chosen) English throughout, matching the given consent wording; Slovenian characters are supported in all data (NFR-01); 2. Slovenian user interface, which would need wording nobody has approved.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review

## D-14: Maximum lengths of text fields
- Timestamp: $T
- Phase: 1
- Type: non-blocking
- Trigger: G-06; no field length is given, but SR-03 needs a body size limit and the database needs column sizes.
- Options: 1. (chosen) 200 characters per name, institution and programme field, 254 for email (RFC 5321 path limit), 50 for student ID, counted after trimming; longer input is rejected with a field error (HTTP 400); request body limit 16 KB; 2. No field limits, body limit only.
- Human response: none
- Resolution: pending review
EOF
python3 - <<EOF
import json
p='03_statistics/run-log.json'; d=json.load(open(p))
for i in ("D-11","D-12","D-13","D-14"):
    d['decisions'].append({"id":i,"type":"non-blocking","phase":1,"category":"requirement","start":"$T","end":None})
json.dump(d,open(p,'w'),indent=2); open(p,'a').write('\n')
EOF

content.text:
Phases 0 and 1 are done and committed, and I've stopped at the phase 1 gate. Phase 2 (design) is next.

**Phase 0 (preflight and setup)**
- **Your answers:** I recorded all of them. Docker Engine 29.3.1, Compose 5.1.1 and the Ubuntu JDK 21.0.12.1 are approved for this run. `vite` is pinned at 6.4.5. `vitest` stays at 4.1.11, with its Moderate advisories accepted.
- **Backend:** builds, and the format, lint and static-analysis checks are clean. The resolved dependency versions match `tech-stack.md`.
- **Frontend:** format, lint, type check, build and test all pass. The lock file matches the exact pins.
- **Backend vulnerability scan:** the NVD-based scan ran. I had to turn off its second data source (Sonatype OSS Index) because it needs a login that isn't in `secrets.env.example` (D-08). The scan found only the two CVEs your pre-approved list already covers (PA-01, PA-02). They're suppressed for those two artifacts only.
- **Frontend audit:** no High is left. The 5 Moderates are in dev tooling only, and the audit of production dependencies alone finds nothing.
- **Secrets:** I checked that the NVD key appears in no log or committed file.
- **Input manifest:** written, covering 51 files.

**Things to know for later phases**
- The Testcontainers database tests can't find Docker on their own, because Docker Desktop's socket isn't at the standard path. Test commands will point them at it, which changes nothing on your machine.
- Node 24.13.0 isn't on your default PATH, so I add the nvm copy to PATH for each command.

Both notes are in `02_output/docs/00_progress.md`.

**Phase 1 (requirements check)**
All 8 stories have acceptance criteria, all 35 criteria and their references check out, and all six open questions have answers. I found four places where the inputs leave something a user would notice undecided. I chose the more cautious option for each and marked it pending review:

| # | Gap | What I chose |
|---|---|---|

# Security baseline

> Owner: Security officer · Read in: phases 0, 2, 6 · Agent: read-only

Applies to every project. Project requirements (`SR-nn`) and the chosen standard level are in `project/02_design/security-requirements.md`.

## Verification standard by component type

| Component type | Standard | Default level |
|---|---|---|
| Web app, API, service | OWASP ASVS (latest) | Level 1; Level 2 when handling authentication, payments or sensitive personal data |
| Mobile app | OWASP MASVS (latest) | L1 |
| Desktop app, CLI, library | Applicable OWASP ASVS chapters | Level 1 |

## Controls for every project

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-01 | All input is validated on the trusted side (server or core), whatever the client does. |
| SB-02 | Every non-public operation checks authentication and authorization. |
| SB-03 | Credentials are stored only as salted, slow hashes; secrets come from configuration (ES-01, ES-02). |
| SB-04 | Data in transit uses TLS outside the local machine. |
| SB-05 | Output is encoded for its context; queries are parameterised. |
| SB-06 | Public and authentication endpoints are rate limited. |
| SB-07 | Errors and logs expose no internals, secrets or personal data (ES-07). |
| SB-08 | Dependencies are scanned; no known Critical or High vulnerability ships. |
| SB-09 | Source is scanned with static analysis and a secret scanner. |
| SB-10 | Web responses carry security headers (content security policy, framing, content-type options). |
| SB-11 | Deployed processes run with least privilege (e.g. non-root containers). |

## Personal data (privacy)

| ID | Control |
|---|---|
| SB-12 | Collect only the personal data a requirement needs; the project lists it. |
| SB-13 | Each personal-data item has a stated purpose and retention period. |
| SB-14 | Consent, where required, is explicit and never preselected. |

openapi: 3.1.0
info:
  title: Conference registration API
  version: 1.0.0
  description: >
    REST API between the frontend (or the organizer) and the backend (AR-01).
    All paths are under /api. Every endpoint is rate limited per client (SR-03) and
    request bodies are limited to 16 KB (D-14); see docs/02_specification.md.
servers:
  - url: /api
paths:
  /form-config:
    get:
      operationId: getFormConfig
      summary: Form configuration with the active options and the consents (AC-003-01)
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Active configuration
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/FormConfig"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ServerError"
  /registrations:
    post:
      operationId: createRegistration
      summary: Submit a registration (US-001, US-002)
      requestBody:
        required: true
        content:
          application/json:
            schema:
              $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationRequest"
      responses:
        "201":
          description: >
            Accepted. Sent only after the database row and the JSON copy are written
            (AR-05). Email failures do not change this status (OQ-03).
          headers:
            Location:
              description: /api/registrations/{id}; not a readable resource, identifies the registration
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationAccepted"
        "400":
          description: Rejected; nothing stored, no email sent
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/ValidationError"
        "413":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/PayloadTooLarge"
        "415":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/UnsupportedMediaType"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ServerError"
  /registrations/export:
    get:
      operationId: exportRegistrations
      summary: Excel export of all registrations, organizers only (US-008, BR-08)
      security:
        - organizerBasic: []
      responses:
        "200":
          description: Workbook with one row per registration
          headers:
            Content-Disposition:
              description: attachment; filename="registrations-<yyyy-MM-dd>.xlsx"
              schema:
                type: string
          content:
            application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet:
              schema:
                type: string
                contentEncoding: binary
        "401":
          description: Missing or wrong credentials (AC-008-02); WWW-Authenticate Basic
          headers:
            WWW-Authenticate:
              schema:
                type: string
                const: Basic realm="registration-export"
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
        "403":
          description: Plain HTTP from a non-localhost client while HTTPS-only access is on (AC-008-04, SR-06, D-11)
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
        "429":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/TooManyRequests"
        "500":
          $ref: "#/components/responses/ServerError"
components:
  securitySchemes:
    organizerBasic:
      type: http
      scheme: basic
  responses:
    TooManyRequests:
      description: Rate limit exceeded (SR-03)
      headers:
        Retry-After:
          schema:
            type: integer
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
    PayloadTooLarge:
      description: Body larger than the limit (SR-03)
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
    UnsupportedMediaType:
      description: Body is not application/json
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
    ServerError:
      description: General error without internal details (SB-07)
      content:
        application/json:
          schema:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/Error"
  schemas:
    RegistrationType:
      type: string
      enum: [EXTERNAL, STUDENT]
    OptionCategory:
      type: string
      enum: [WORKSHOP, EVENT, MEAL, OTHER]
    FormConfig:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [conferenceName, captcha, options, consents]
      properties:
        conferenceName:
          type: string
        captcha:
          type: object
          additionalProperties: false
          required: [mode]
          properties:
            mode:
              type: string
              enum: [RECAPTCHA, TEST]
              description: TEST only when the environment enables reCAPTCHA test mode (SR-02)
            siteKey:
              type: string
              description: Present when mode is RECAPTCHA; the only key the frontend receives (AR-07)
        options:
          type: array
          description: Active options only (BR-04), in configuration order
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/FormOption"
        consents:
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/FormConsent"
    FormOption:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, name, category, availableTo]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
        name:
          type: string
        category:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/OptionCategory"
        availableTo:
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          uniqueItems: true
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
    FormConsent:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, text, mandatory]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
        text:
          type: string
        mandatory:
          type: boolean
    RegistrationRequest:
      type: object
      description: >
        Structural schema. Business validation (required per type, trimming, email format,
        lengths, options, consents, captcha) is done by the backend and reported as field
        errors, so missing or wrong fields give 400 with ValidationError, not a parse error.
        Fields of the other registration type must be absent or empty.
      properties:
        type:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
        firstName:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
        lastName:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
        email:
          type: string
          maxLength: 254
        organization:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
          description: EXTERNAL only
        studyInstitution:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
          description: STUDENT only
        studyProgramme:
          type: string
          maxLength: 200
          description: STUDENT only
        studentId:
          type: string
          maxLength: 50
          description: STUDENT only
        optionIds:
          type: array
          items:
            type: string
        consents:
          type: array
          description: Ids of the consents the participant gave
          items:
            type: string
        recaptchaToken:
          type: string
    RegistrationAccepted:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [id, registeredAt, type, firstName, lastName, options]
      properties:
        id:
          type: string
          format: uuid
        registeredAt:
          type: string
          format: date-time
        type:
          $ref: "#/components/schemas/RegistrationType"
        firstName:
          type: string
        lastName:
          type: string
        options:
          type: array
          items:
            type: object
            additionalProperties: false
            required: [id, name, category]
            properties:
              id:
                type: string
              name:
                type: string
              category:
                $ref: "#/components/schemas/OptionCategory"
    FieldError:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [field, code, message]
      properties:
        field:
          type: string
          description: >
            One of type, firstName, lastName, email, organization, studyInstitution,
            studyProgramme, studentId, optionIds, consents.<consentId>, recaptchaToken
        code:
          type: string
          enum: [REQUIRED, INVALID_FORMAT, TOO_LONG, NOT_ALLOWED, UNKNOWN_OPTION, INACTIVE_OPTION, DUPLICATE_OPTION, OPTION_NOT_AVAILABLE, CONSENT_REQUIRED, UNKNOWN_CONSENT, CAPTCHA_FAILED]
        message:
          type: string
    ValidationError:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [message, fieldErrors]
      properties:
        message:
          type: string
        fieldErrors:
          type: array
          minItems: 1
          items:
            $ref: "#/components/schemas/FieldError"
    Error:
      type: object
      additionalProperties: false
      required: [message]
      properties:
        message:
          type: string

-- Contract: registration storage between the backend and PostgreSQL (BR-07, AR-06).
-- The Flyway migration V1 creates exactly this schema; later changes are new migrations.
-- Lengths follow D-14. Option and consent texts are stored as accepted, so the export
-- stays correct after the configuration changes (AR-04).

CREATE TABLE registration (
    id                 UUID         PRIMARY KEY,
    type               VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('EXTERNAL', 'STUDENT')),
    first_name         VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    last_name          VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    email              VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL,
    organization       VARCHAR(200),
    study_institution  VARCHAR(200),
    study_programme    VARCHAR(200),
    student_id         VARCHAR(50),
    registered_at      TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT registration_fields_by_type CHECK (
        (type = 'EXTERNAL' AND organization IS NOT NULL
            AND study_institution IS NULL AND study_programme IS NULL AND student_id IS NULL)
        OR
        (type = 'STUDENT' AND organization IS NULL
            AND study_institution IS NOT NULL AND study_programme IS NOT NULL AND student_id IS NOT NULL)
    )
);

CREATE INDEX registration_registered_at_idx ON registration (registered_at);

CREATE TABLE registration_option (
    registration_id  UUID         NOT NULL REFERENCES registration (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    position         INTEGER      NOT NULL,
    option_id        VARCHAR(64)  NOT NULL,
    option_name      VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    category         VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL CHECK (category IN ('WORKSHOP', 'EVENT', 'MEAL', 'OTHER')),
    PRIMARY KEY (registration_id, option_id),
    UNIQUE (registration_id, position)
);

CREATE TABLE registration_consent (
    registration_id  UUID          NOT NULL REFERENCES registration (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    consent_id       VARCHAR(64)   NOT NULL,
    consent_text     VARCHAR(1000) NOT NULL,
    given_at         TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (registration_id, consent_id)
);

# Email contract

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03 · Agent: writes

Interface between the backend and the SMTP server. Both messages are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist (AR-05, OQ-03), one SMTP message per recipient. A send failure is logged as `registration <id>: <participant|organizer> email not sent` with no personal data or exception text containing addresses (ES-07) and does not change the 201 response (AC-006-03).

## Common rules (SR-05)

- `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8` only, never HTML: markup in user input appears as literal text (AC-006-02).
- The subject contains only configured text (conference name) and never user input.
- The only user-supplied header value is the participant's `To` address, which has already passed the email validation (one address, no CR/LF, no comma-separated list) and is set as a single parsed `InternetAddress`.
- User text in the body has CR and LF replaced by a space before it is written, so a value cannot add lines that look like other fields.
- `From`: `MAIL_FROM`. No `Cc`, `Bcc` or `Reply-To`.

## Participant confirmation (US-006)

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| To | the participant's email |
| Subject | `Registration confirmed: <conference name>` |
| Body | Conference name; `Dear <first name> <last name>,`; registration id; registration type (`External participant` / `Student`); selected option names grouped by category (Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities), or `No options selected.` |

## Organizer notification (US-007)

| Part | Content |
|---|---|
| To | each address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` (one message each) |
| Subject | `New registration: <conference name>` |
| Body | Registration id, type, registration time (UTC, ISO 8601), every participant field with its label, selected options by category, consents with the time given. Only registration data (SR-07). |
| Attachment | `registration-<id>.json`, `application/json; charset=UTF-8`, the exact bytes of the stored JSON copy (AC-007-02) |

# Registration form UI contract

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-001, US-002, US-004, BR-01..06, NFR-03, D-13 · Agent: writes

Interface between the participant and the frontend. Text is English (D-13). Element names below are the accessible names that tests use (`getByRole`, `getByLabel`), so they are part of the contract.

## Page states

| State | Shown |
|---|---|
| Loading | `Loading…` while `GET /api/form-config` runs |
| Configuration error | Alert `The registration form is not available right now. Please try again later.` |
| Choose type | Heading `Conference registration` with the conference name; radio group `Registration type` with `External participant` and `Student`, none selected; no form fields |
| Form | Fields of the chosen type, options, consents, captcha, button `Register` |
| Submitting | `Register` disabled |
| Confirmation (AC-004-01) | Heading `Registration received`; text `Thank you, <first name> <last name>.`; list `Selected options` with each option name, or `No options selected.`; the form is not rendered |

## Fields (BR-01)

| Label | Type | External | Student | Max length (D-14) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `First name` | text | yes | yes | 200 |
| `Last name` | text | yes | yes | 200 |
| `Email` | email | yes | yes | 254 |
| `Organization / institution` | text | yes | no | 200 |
| `Study institution` | text | no | yes | 200 |
| `Study programme` | text | no | yes | 200 |
| `Student ID` | text | no | yes | 50 |

Switching type keeps the shared fields (names, email) and clears the selected options that the new type cannot use.

## Options (BR-04, OQ-01)

One group (`fieldset`) per category, in this order and with these legends: `Workshops`, `Events`, `Meals`, `Other activities`. Each active option available to the chosen type is a checkbox labelled with its display name, unchecked at first. A category with no option for the type is not rendered.

## Consents (BR-05, OQ-02)

One checkbox per configured consent, labelled with its text, never preselected (AC-001-08, AC-002-07). A mandatory consent is marked `(required)`.

## Captcha (SR-01, SR-02)

- Mode `RECAPTCHA`: the Google reCAPTCHA v2 checkbox widget, rendered with the site key from the form configuration.
- Mode `TEST`: a checkbox labelled `I am not a robot (test mode)`; checked sends token `test-pass`.

## Validation and errors (NFR-03, AC-004-02..04)

- Before sending, the frontend checks every required field of the type (after trimming), the email format, the lengths, the mandatory consents and that a captcha token exists. On any error it sends no request (AC-004-03).
- Each field error is shown under its field as text linked with `aria-describedby`, and the field gets `aria-invalid="true"`. Option errors are shown under the options, consent errors under that consent, captcha errors under the captcha.
- Backend field errors (400) are mapped by `field` to the same places; the entered values stay (AC-004-02).
- Any other failure (5xx, 413, 429, network error, unreadable response) shows the alert `Your registration could not be sent. Please try again later.` with no technical detail and keeps the values (AC-004-04, SB-07).

| Code | Message shown |
|---|---|
| REQUIRED | `This field is required.` |
| INVALID_FORMAT | `Enter a valid email address.` |
| TOO_LONG | `This value is too long.` |
| UNKNOWN_OPTION, INACTIVE_OPTION, DUPLICATE_OPTION, OPTION_NOT_AVAILABLE, NOT_ALLOWED | `One or more selected options are not available.` (options) / `This field is not allowed for this registration type.` (fields) |
| CONSENT_REQUIRED | `This consent is required.` |
| UNKNOWN_CONSENT | `This consent is not available.` |
| CAPTCHA_FAILED | `Please confirm that you are not a robot.` |

);

> Written in: phase 2 · Source: US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03 · Agent: writes

Interface between the backend and the SMTP server. Both messages are sent only after the database row and the JSON copy exist (AR-05, OQ-03), one SMTP message per recipient. ## Common rules (SR-05)

- `Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8` only, never HTML: markup in user input appears as literal text (AC-006-02).

## S1 Components

| Component | Folder | Role |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot REST API under `/api`, PostgreSQL via JPA, JSON copies on a volume, SMTP, Excel export |
| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React single page served by nginx; talks to the backend only through `/api` (AR-01) |
| local stack | `02_output/docker-compose.yml` | backend, frontend, PostgreSQL, Mailpit (`environments.md`, local) |

## S2 Backend architecture (AR-02, AR-03)

Ports and adapters, so that the business rules are testable without Spring and every external system sits behind an interface. Packages under `si.konferenca.registration`:

| Package | Contains | May depend on |
|---|---|---|
| `domain` | Registration model, registration types, option and consent definitions, validation rules, field errors | JDK only |
| `application` | Use cases (`RegisterParticipant`, `GetFormConfiguration`, `ExportRegistrations`) and the ports they call (`RegistrationStore`, `JsonCopyStore`, `CaptchaVerifier`, `RegistrationNotifier`, `RegistrationWorkbook`) | `domain`; Spring `stereotype` and `transaction` annotations |
| `config` | Loading and checking the conference configuration and the typed application settings | `domain`, Spring |
| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `RegistrationStore` implementation | `application`, `domain`, JPA |
| `adapter.jsoncopy` | `JsonCopyStore` on the file system | `application`, `domain` |
| `adapter.captcha` | Google siteverify client and test-mode verifier | `application`, `config` |
| `adapter.mail` | `RegistrationNotifier` with Spring Mail | `application`, `domain`, `config` |
| `adapter.export` | `RegistrationWorkbook` with Apache POI | `application`, `domain` |
| `web` | Controllers, request and response DTOs, error mapping, security, rate-limit and size filters | `application`, `domain`, `config` |

ArchUnit rules, which check exactly this declaration:

1. `domain` depends on no other project package and on no `org.springframework..`, `jakarta.persistence..` or `org.apache.poi..` class.
2. `application` depends only on `domain` among project packages.
3. No `adapter..` package depends on `web`, and no adapter depends on another adapter.
4. `web` depends on no `adapter..` package.
5. No package cycles between the top-level slices of `si.konferenca.registration` (AR-03).

## S3 API (`openapi.yaml`)

### S3.1 `GET /api/form-config`

Returns the conference name, the captcha mode and site key, the active options (each with id, name, category and `availableTo`), and the consents. Inactive options are never included (AC-003-01).

### S3.2 `POST /api/registrations`

The JSON body follows `RegistrationRequest`. It is validated in full, and all field errors are returned together as `400 ValidationError`. On acceptance the response is `201` with a `Location` header and `RegistrationAccepted`, which holds the UUID id, time, type, names and selected options. The status and error shapes are the ones in the contract: 413 for a body over 16 KB, 415 when the body is not JSON, 429 for the rate limit, and 500 with a general message.

### S3.3 `GET /api/registrations/export`

HTTP Basic for the organizer role (S7.2). The response is an `.xlsx` (S4.8).

## S4 Registration processing (backend, SB-01)

Order in `RegisterParticipant`: validate fields, options and consents (S4.2..S4.4), then verify the captcha (S4.5), then store (S4.6), then notify (S4.7). The captcha is verified last, so an invalid form does not use up a token. Every check runs before anything is written. A rejected submission writes no row and no JSON copy, and sends no email.

### S4.1 Types (BR-01)

`EXTERNAL` takes first name, last name, email and organization. `STUDENT` takes first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme and student ID. A missing or unknown `type` gives the field error `type`/`REQUIRED`. A non-blank field of the other type gives `<field>`/`NOT_ALLOWED`.

### S4.2 Fields (BR-02, BR-03, D-14)

- Each text value is trimmed with `String.strip()` (Unicode whitespace) before any check, and only the trimmed value is stored (AC-001-03).
- A field that is missing, null, empty or blank after trimming gives `REQUIRED` (AC-001-02, AC-002-02).
- Lengths are counted in Unicode code points after trimming: 200 for names, organization, study institution and programme; 254 for email; 50 for student ID. A longer value gives `TOO_LONG`.
- Email: one address of the form `local@domain`. The local part is 1..64 characters from `A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_\`{|}~.-`, with no leading, trailing or double dot. The domain has at least two labels of `A-Za-z0-9-`, does not start or end a label with `-`, and its last label is at least two letters. No spaces, CR, LF or commas are allowed. Anything else gives `INVALID_FORMAT` (AC-001-04, AC-002-03). The same rule runs in the frontend (S6.2).
- Text accepts any Unicode letters, including č, š, ž (BR-03). Control characters other than tab are rejected with `INVALID_FORMAT` in name, institution, programme and student ID fields.

### S4.3 Options (BR-04, SR-04, OQ-01, OQ-04)

`optionIds` may be absent or empty. Each id must exist in the configuration (`UNKNOWN_OPTION`), be active (`INACTIVE_OPTION`) and be available to the type (`OPTION_NOT_AVAILABLE`, applied to both types, G-01). An id listed twice gives `DUPLICATE_OPTION`. All option errors use the field `optionIds`. There is no limit per category.

### S4.4 Consents (BR-05, OQ-02)

`consents` lists the ids the participant gave. Every mandatory consent must be present, otherwise the error is `consents.<id>`/`CONSENT_REQUIRED`. An id that is not configured gives `consents.<id>`/`UNKNOWN_CONSENT`. Each given consent is stored with the registration time as its `givenAt`.

### S4.5 Captcha (SR-01, SR-02, AR-07, DoD-P05)

- `CaptchaVerifier` is always called on the backend. A missing or blank token, or a rejected one, gives `recaptchaToken`/`CAPTCHA_FAILED` (400, nothing stored; AC-001-07, AC-002-06).
- Production verifier: POST to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default Google siteverify) with the secret and the token, with a 5 s connect and read timeout. The token is accepted only on HTTP 200 with `success: true` (`recaptcha-siteverify.schema.json`). Tests run this path against a mock HTTP server, including a rejected token and an error status.
- Test mode (`RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE=true`): no network call. Token `test-pass` is accepted and anything else is rejected. The form configuration reports `captcha.mode = TEST`.
- At startup, `APP_ENVIRONMENT=production` with test mode on, or with an empty site or secret key, stops the application (SR-02). Test mode is off unless the variable sets it.
- The site key is the only key sent to the frontend. The secret stays in the backend (AR-07).

### S4.6 Storage (BR-07, AR-05, AR-06)

1. One database transaction inserts the `registration` row with its options (id, name and category as accepted) and consents (`database-schema.sql`), then flushes.
2. Still inside the transaction, the JSON copy (`registration-copy.schema.json`) is written as UTF-8 to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.tmp`, forced to disk, and moved atomically to `<id>.json`.
3. If step 2 fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 with a general message. No row is left (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after step 2, the file is deleted.
4. Only after the commit does the use case return the accepted registration, so the 201 always means both copies exist (AR-05).

The schema is created only by Flyway migration `V1__create_registration.sql`, which equals `database-schema.sql`, with Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate` (AR-06, ES-08). Queries go through JPA, so they are parameterised (SB-05). Ids are random UUIDs. JSON is written by Jackson. The database uses UTF-8 encoding, so text is stored unchanged (AC-005-04).

### S4.7 Emails (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03)

After the commit, the backend sends the participant confirmation and one notification per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, synchronously, with SMTP connect, read and write timeouts of 5 s. Each send is wrapped separately. A failure is logged with the registration id only, and the response is still 201 (AC-006-03). The content and the injection rules are in `emails.md`: plain text only, a fixed subject, the parsed single `To` address, and CR/LF in body values replaced. The attachment is the stored JSON copy byte for byte (AC-007-02).

### S4.8 Export (US-008, SR-07, AC-008-01, AC-008-03)

There is one sheet, `Registrations`, with a header row and one row per registration ordered by registration time. Columns: Registration ID, Type, Registered at (UTC, ISO 8601), First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (option names joined with `; `), and Consents (`<id> (<givenAt>)` joined with `; `). Every cell is written as a string cell (`setCellValue(String)`), never as a formula. Text therefore stays unchanged (AC-008-03), and a value such as `=1+1` is not evaluated. The workbook includes no internal field (SR-07). The file name is `registrations-<yyyy-MM-dd>.xlsx`.

## S5 Conference configuration (AR-04, US-003, OQ-01, OQ-02)

- The options and consents come from the JSON file named by `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE`, which follows `conference-config.schema.json`. The conference name comes from `CONFERENCE_NAME`. The file is read once at startup, so changing the file and restarting changes the form with no code change (AC-003-02). The participant fields (BR-01) cannot be configured.

- `availableTo` defaults to both types (OQ-01).

React 19 with TypeScript, built by Vite and served as static files. One page: `App` loads the form configuration, `TypeChooser` picks the type, `RegistrationForm` shows the fields, `OptionGroups`, `Consents` and `Captcha`, `Confirmation` shows the result, and `api.ts` is the only module that calls `fetch`, only on relative `/api/...` paths (AR-01). The frontend holds no secret. The reCAPTCHA site key comes from the form configuration (AR-07). React escapes rendered text (SB-05), and no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is used.

### S6.1 Form (AC-001-08, AC-002-07)

The form shows exactly the fields of the chosen type. It lists the active options for that type in the four category groups, all unchecked, and every consent unchecked.

### S6.2 Submission and messages (BR-06, NFR-03, AC-004-01..04)

- The frontend validates with the same rules as S4.2 to S4.4 (required, trim, email, lengths, mandatory consents, captcha token present). If anything fails, it shows field errors and sends nothing (AC-004-03).
- On 201 it replaces the form with the confirmation, using the name and options from the response (AC-004-01, BR-06).
- On 400 it shows each `fieldErrors` entry at its field and keeps the values (AC-004-02).
- On any other status or a network error it shows the general alert from the UI contract and keeps the values (AC-004-04).

## S7 Cross-cutting backend behaviour

### S7.1 Configuration (ES-01)

| Variable | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `APP_ENVIRONMENT` | `local`, `test` or `production` | none (required) |
| `DATABASE_URL`, `DATABASE_USERNAME`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` | Database | none (compose sets local values) |
| `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_STARTTLS` | Mail server; STARTTLS required when true | none (compose sets Mailpit) |
| `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | Mail account, optional | empty |
| `MAIL_FROM` | Sender address | `registration@localhost` |
| `CONFERENCE_NAME` | Shown in the form and emails | `Conference` |
| `CONFERENCE_CONFIG_FILE` | Options and consents file | none (compose mounts `config/conference.json`) |
| `JSON_COPY_DIR` | Directory for JSON copies on a persistent volume | `/data/json-copies` |
| `RECAPTCHA_TEST_MODE` | Test mode | `false` |
| `RECAPTCHA_SITE_KEY`, `RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY` | Keys | empty; production refuses empty |
| `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` | Verify endpoint | `https://www.google.com/recaptcha/api/siteverify` |
| `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` | Organizer credentials | none (required) |
| `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` | Notification recipients, comma separated | none (required) |
| `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY` | SR-06 check | `true` |
| `CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGIN` | Allowed origin for the Vite dev server | empty (no CORS) |
| `RATE_LIMIT_FORM_CONFIG_PER_MINUTE`, `RATE_LIMIT_REGISTRATION_PER_MINUTE`, `RATE_LIMIT_EXPORT_PER_MINUTE` | Per-client limits | 60, 10, 10 |
| `MAX_REQUEST_BYTES` | Body limit | 16384 |

### S7.2 Organizer access (BR-08, SB-02, SB-03, SR-06, D-11)

- Spring Security, stateless, with no session and no cookies. CSRF protection is therefore off: no endpoint relies on ambient credentials. `/api/form-config` and `POST /api/registrations` are public. `GET /api/registrations/export` requires the role `ORGANIZER` through HTTP Basic. `/actuator/health/**` is public. Everything else is denied.
- At startup the password from `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` is hashed with BCrypt (strength 12). Only the hash is kept in memory, and comparisons use the BCrypt encoder (SB-03).
- A missing or wrong credential gives 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Basic realm="registration-export"` and an `Error` body with no data (AC-008-02).
- HTTPS-only check (SR-06, AC-008-04): when `ORGANIZER_HTTPS_ONLY=true` and a request to the export arrives that is not secure (`request.isSecure()` after the trusted `X-Forwarded-Proto`) from a client address that is not loopback, the backend answers 403 `Error` before it reads the credentials, with no redirect (D-11). Tomcat's `RemoteIpValve` (`server.forward-headers-strategy=native`) trusts forwarded headers only from the default internal proxy ranges.

### S7.3 Rate and size limits (SR-03, SB-06)

- A servlet filter before security gives each client address (after `RemoteIpValve`) a fixed-window counter per endpoint group: form configuration, registration and export, with the limits in S7.1. Requests over the limit get 429 with `Retry-After`. Failed and successful export logins count together, which limits password guessing. Counters live in memory, and stale entries are dropped every window.

A `@RestControllerAdvice` maps validation to 400 `ValidationError`, unreadable JSON to 400 with the field `type`/`REQUIRED`, wrong media type to 415, and anything else to 500 `{"message":"The request could not be processed."}`. Nothing else is shown: no stack trace and no exception text. Logs contain registration ids, never names, emails or request bodies. Spring's default error pages are disabled.

### S7.5 Security headers (SB-10)

- API responses (Spring Security): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; frame-ancestors 'none'`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`, and `Cache-Control: no-store` on the export.
- Frontend (nginx): `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://www.gstatic.com/recaptcha/; frame-src https://www.google.com/recaptcha/ https://recaptcha.google.com/recaptcha/; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:; connect-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'`, plus `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

## S8 Deployment and runtime

- Backend image: a multi-stage build that packages with the Maven wrapper and runs on `eclipse-temurin:21.0.10_7-jre-alpine` as a non-root user (uid 10001), with a read-only JSON copy mount only for the configuration (SB-11).
- Frontend image: builds in `node:24.13.0-alpine` and serves from `nginx:1.30.5-alpine` as non-root on port 8080. Its nginx serves `/` and proxies `/api/` to the backend. It sets `proxy_set_header Host` to the upstream itself and never forwards the client's Host (SR-08). It sets `X-Forwarded-For $remote_addr`, replacing rather than appending, and `X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme`.
- `docker-compose.yml` (local): `postgres:16.15-alpine`, `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1`, backend and frontend. It publishes only `127.0.0.1:8080` (frontend) and `127.0.0.1:8025` (Mailpit UI and API), and uses named volumes `pgdata` and `json-copies` (NFR-02). ## S9 Personal data and localisation (SB-12..14, NFR-01)

- Only the fields in `business-rules.md` "Data" and the consents with their time are collected. Their purposes and retention are as in `security-requirements.md` and OQ-06: kept until the operator deletes them, and the release notes ask for deletion within 12 months. Consents are never preselected, and a given consent is stored with its time (SB-14).

## S10 Quality and security tooling

Every tool is as listed in `tech-stack.md`. Backend checks: Spotless, PMD, SpotBugs, JaCoCo, PIT and Dependency-Check. Frontend checks: Prettier, ESLint, tsc, Vitest with v8 coverage, Stryker, jscpd and npm audit. Both components also run Semgrep and Gitleaks, and use Playwright for the end-to-end scenarios against the local stack (DoD-P01..P04). The levels of the acceptance tests are defined in phase 3 (`docs/03_test-strategy.md`).

Returns the conference name, the captcha mode and site key, the active options (each with id, name, category and `availableTo`), and the consents. Inactive options are never included (AC-003-01).

### S3.2 `POST /api/registrations`

The JSON body follows `RegistrationRequest`. It is validated in full, and all field errors are returned together as `400 ValidationError`. On acceptance the response is `201` with a `Location` header and `RegistrationAccepted`, which holds the UUID id, time, type, names and selected options. The status and error shapes are the ones in the contract: 413 for a body over 16 KB, 415 when the body is not JSON, 429 for the rate limit, and 500 with a general message.

HTTP Basic for the organizer role (S7.2). The response is an `.xlsx` (S4.8).

## S4 Registration processing (backend, SB-01)

Order in `RegisterParticipant`: validate fields, options and consents (S4.2..S4.4), then verify the captcha (S4.5), then store (S4.6), then notify (S4.7). The captcha is verified last, so an invalid form does not use up a token. Every check runs before anything is written. A rejected submission writes no row and no JSON copy, and sends no email.

### S4.1 Types (BR-01)

`EXTERNAL` takes first name, last name, email and organization. `STUDENT` takes first name, last name, email, study institution, study programme and student ID. A missing or unknown `type` gives the field error `type`/`REQUIRED`. A non-blank field of the other type gives `<field>`/`NOT_ALLOWED`.

### S4.2 Fields (BR-02, BR-03, D-14)

- Each text value is trimmed with `String.strip()` (Unicode whitespace) before any check, and only the trimmed value is stored (AC-001-03).
- A field that is missing, null, empty or blank after trimming gives `REQUIRED` (AC-001-02, AC-002-02).
- Lengths are counted in Unicode code points after trimming: 200 for names, organization, study institution and programme; 254 for email; 50 for student ID. A longer value gives `TOO_LONG`.
- Email: one address of the form `local@domain`. The local part is 1..64 characters from `A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_\`{|}~.-`, with no leading, trailing or double dot. The domain has at least two labels of `A-Za-z0-9-`, does not start or end a label with `-`, and its last label is at least two letters. No spaces, CR, LF or commas are allowed. Anything else gives `INVALID_FORMAT` (AC-001-04, AC-002-03). The same rule runs in the frontend (S6.2).
- Text accepts any Unicode letters, including č, š, ž (BR-03). Control characters other than tab are rejected with `INVALID_FORMAT` in name, institution, programme and student ID fields.

### S4.3 Options (BR-04, SR-04, OQ-01, OQ-04)

`optionIds` may be absent or empty. Each id must exist in the configuration (`UNKNOWN_OPTION`), be active (`INACTIVE_OPTION`) and be available to the type (`OPTION_NOT_AVAILABLE`, applied to both types, G-01). An id listed twice gives `DUPLICATE_OPTION`. All option errors use the field `optionIds`. There is no limit per category.

### S4.4 Consents (BR-05, OQ-02)

`consents` lists the ids the participant gave. Every mandatory consent must be present, otherwise the error is `consents.<id>`/`CONSENT_REQUIRED`. An id that is not configured gives `consents.<id>`/`UNKNOWN_CONSENT`. Each given consent is stored with the registration time as its `givenAt`.

### S4.5 Captcha (SR-01, SR-02, AR-07, DoD-P05)

- `CaptchaVerifier` is always called on the backend. A missing or blank token, or a rejected one, gives `recaptchaToken`/`CAPTCHA_FAILED` (400, nothing stored; AC-001-07, AC-002-06).
- Production verifier: POST to `RECAPTCHA_VERIFY_URL` (default Google siteverify) with the secret and the token, with a 5 s connect and read timeout. - The site key is the only key sent to the frontend. The secret stays in the backend (AR-07).

1. One database transaction inserts the `registration` row with its options (id, name and category as accepted) and consents (`database-schema.sql`), then flushes.
2. Still inside the transaction, the JSON copy (`registration-copy.schema.json`) is written as UTF-8 to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.tmp`, forced to disk, and moved atomically to `<id>.json`.
3. If step 2 fails, the transaction rolls back and the API answers 500 with a general message. No row is left (AC-005-03). If the commit fails after step 2, the file is deleted.
4. Only after the commit does the use case return the accepted registration, so the 201 always means both copies exist (AR-05).

The schema is created only by Flyway migration `V1__create_registration.sql`, which equals `database-schema.sql`, with Hibernate `ddl-auto=validate` (AR-06, ES-08). Queries go through JPA, so they are parameterised (SB-05). Ids are random UUIDs. JSON is written by Jackson. The database uses UTF-8 encoding, so text is stored unchanged (AC-005-04).

### S4.7 Emails (US-006, US-007, SR-05, SR-07, OQ-03)

After the commit, the backend sends the participant confirmation and one notification per address in `ORGANIZER_EMAILS`, synchronously, with SMTP connect, read and write timeouts of 5 s. The content and the injection rules are in `emails.md`: plain text only, a fixed subject, the parsed single `To` address, and CR/LF in body values replaced. The attachment is the stored JSON copy byte for byte (AC-007-02).

### S4.8 Export (US-008, SR-07, AC-008-01, AC-008-03)

There is one sheet, `Registrations`, with a header row and one row per registration ordered by registration time. Columns: Registration ID, Type, Registered at (UTC, ISO 8601), First name, Last name, Email, Organization / institution, Study institution, Study programme, Student ID, Workshops, Events, Meals, Other activities (option names joined with `; `), and Consents (`<id> (<givenAt>)` joined with `; `). +| backend | `02_output/backend` | Spring Boot REST API under `/api`, PostgreSQL via JPA, JSON copies on a volume, SMTP, Excel export |
+| frontend | `02_output/frontend` | React single page served by nginx; talks to the backend only through `/api` (AR-01) |

+| `domain` | Registration model, registration types, option and consent definitions, validation rules, field errors | JDK only |

+| `adapter.persistence` | JPA entities, Spring Data repositories, `RegistrationStore` implementation | `application`, `domain`, JPA |
+| `adapter.captcha` | Google siteverify client and test-mode verifier | `application`, `config` |
+| `web` | Controllers, request and response DTOs, error mapping, security, rate-limit and size filters | `application`, `domain`, `config` |

+2. `application` depends only on `domain` among project packages.
+3. No `adapter..` package depends on `web`, and no adapter depends on another adapter.
+5. No package cycles between the top-level slices of `si.konferenca.registration` (AR-03).
+Returns the conference name, the captcha mode and site key, the active options (each with id, name, category and `availableTo`), and the consents. Inactive options are never included (AC-003-01).

+The JSON body follows `RegistrationRequest`. It is validated in full, and all field errors are returned together as `400 ValidationError`. On acceptance the response is `201` with a `Location` header and `RegistrationAccepted`, which holds the UUID id, time, type, names and selected options. The status and error shapes are the ones in the contract: 413 for a body over 16 KB, 415 when the body is not JSON, 429 for the rate limit, and 500 with a general message.
+HTTP Basic for the organizer role (S7.2). The response is an `.xlsx` (S4.8).

+Order in `RegisterParticipant`: validate fields, options and consents (S4.2..S4.4), then verify the captcha (S4.5), then store (S4.6), then notify (S4.7). The captcha is verified last, so an invalid form does not use up a token. Every check runs before anything is written. A rejected submission writes no row and no JSON copy, and sends no email.

+2. Still inside the transaction, the JSON copy (`registration-copy.schema.json`) is written as UTF-8 to `<JSON_COPY_DIR>/<id>.tmp`, forced to disk, and moved atomically to `<id>.json`.

+4. Only after the commit does the use case return the accepted registration, so the 201 always means both copies exist (AR-05).

=== 01_input/00_general/quality/test-strategy.md
# Test strategy

> Owner: QA lead · Read in: every phase that writes or runs tests · Agent: read-only

When each test level is written and whether it is frozen is defined in `general/phases.md`. Project thresholds are in `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md`.

## Constraints

- Do not test acceptance behaviour through internals; use the component's public interface (API, UI, CLI, messages).
- Do not depend on live external services in automated tests; use the local substitutes in `project/00_setup/environments.md` and list the real services in the release notes for manual testing.
- Do not leave flaky, skipped or disabled tests; fix them or record a decision.
- Do not weaken an assertion to make an incorrect implementation pass.

Always record the raw score next to the adjusted score.

## Mutation run discipline

- Measure coverage and mutation score in phase 5, so that surviving mutants are handled before verification. Phase 6 repeats a measurement only for a component whose code or tests changed since, and only once, after the last fix.

lines: - A field that is missing, null, empty or blank after trimming gives `REQUIRED` (AC-001-02, AC-002-02).
- Lengths are counted in Unicode code points after trimming: 200 for names, organization, study institution and programme; 254 for email; 50 for student ID. A longer value gives `TOO_LONG`.

- Email: one address of the form `local@domain`. The local part is 1..64 characters from `A-Za-z0-9!#$%&'*+/=?^_\`{|}~.-`, with no leading, trailing or double dot. The domain has at least two labels of `A-Za-z0-9-`, does not start or end a label with `-`, and its last label is at least two letters. No spaces, CR, LF or commas are allowed. Anything else gives `INVALID_FORMAT` (AC-001-04, AC-002-03). The same rule runs in the frontend (S6.2).

# Test strategy (as executed)

> Written in: the test phases of the selected workflow, and phase 6 · Source: `general/quality/test-strategy.md`, workflow `rules.md` · Agent: writes

## Test levels as executed

| Level | Component | Location | Runner and harness | Frozen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Acceptance | backend | `02_output/backend/src/test/java/si/konferenca/registration/acceptance/` | JUnit 6 through Surefire (`./mvnw -B test`). The real backend on a random port (`@SpringBootTest`) is called over HTTP with `java.net.http.HttpClient`. PostgreSQL `postgres:16.15-alpine` and Mailpit `axllent/mailpit:v1.31.1` run as Testcontainers. The siteverify mock is the JDK `HttpServer`. Configuration is supplied only under the variable names of specification S7.1. Outcomes are read through the public interfaces: the HTTP API, the storage contract (`database-schema.sql`, plain JDBC), the JSON copy directory and the Mailpit API. | yes |
| Acceptance | frontend | `02_output/frontend/src/acceptance/` | Vitest 4 with jsdom and Testing Library. `App` is rendered and driven by accessible role and name, as in `registration-form-ui.md`. `fetch` is stubbed with the contract shapes of `openapi.yaml`. | yes |
| End-to-end | local stack | `02_output/frontend/e2e/` | Playwright 1.63 Chromium against `docker compose up` in `02_output`, with one test per scenario E2E-01..E2E-05. Storage is checked with `docker compose exec` (psql, the JSON copy), mail through the Mailpit API, and the workbook with a built-in zip reader. | yes |
| Architecture | backend | written in phase 4/5 (ArchUnit rules of specification S2) | JUnit | no |
| Unit / integration | both | phase 5 | JUnit, Vitest | no |

The frozen set is every file under the `acceptance` and `e2e` paths above, including their `support/` harness files. It is listed in `docs/03_acceptance-manifest.sha256`. Supporting files that are not frozen: `docker-compose.yml`, the Dockerfiles, `nginx.conf`, `config/conference.json`, `playwright.config.ts` and `vite.config.ts`.

### Running

- Backend: `cd 02_output/backend && ./mvnw -B test`. It needs Docker; Testcontainers finds Docker Desktop by itself. The tests must not run as root, because AC-005-03 makes a directory read-only and asserts that it is.
- Frontend: `cd 02_output/frontend && nvm use && npm test`.
- End-to-end: first `./backend/mvnw -B -f backend/pom.xml package -DskipTests`, then `docker compose --env-file ../.env up -d --build --wait` in `02_output`. Then, in `02_output/frontend`, export `ORGANIZER_USERNAME`, `ORGANIZER_PASSWORD` and `ORGANIZER_EMAILS` from `.env` without printing them (`working-rules.md`, Secrets) and run `npx playwright test`. `E2E_BASE_URL` and `E2E_MAILPIT_URL` override `http://127.0.0.1:8080` and `:8025`. In this run they were `:18080` and `:18025`, because another local project holds 8080 and 8025. `FRONTEND_HOST_PORT` and `MAILPIT_HOST_PORT` move the published ports.

### Choices the tests make (from the specification, not new behaviour)

- "Rejected" is checked as 400, the expected `fieldErrors[].field`, no row, an empty JSON copy directory and no message in Mailpit (`AcceptanceTestBase.assertRejected`).
- AC-001-07 and AC-002-06 run in test mode (token `test-fail`) and also on the production path against the mocked siteverify (`RecaptchaVerificationAcceptanceTest`, DoD-P05). The production path covers an accepted token, a rejected token, an HTTP 500 from the verifier, and the test-mode token while test mode is off.
- AC-005-03 makes the JSON copy directory read-only during the request and expects a 5xx with no row (specification S4.6).
- AC-008-04 sends the request through the trusted proxy headers (`X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.10`). It first checks a control: the same client with `X-Forwarded-Proto: https` gets 200. The plain-HTTP request must then get a 4xx with no data. The exact status is not frozen, because D-11 is pending review.
- AC-003-02 and AC-003-03 start a second backend instance with another configuration file. AC-003-03 passes only if startup throws.
- E2E-03 makes the real backend reject a submission by adding the inactive `ws-legacy` to the form configuration the browser receives (`page.route`). The backend answers `INACTIVE_OPTION`.
- E2E-05 creates its own registration through the API first, so it does not depend on the order of the tests.

### Notes for the implementation (phase 4)

- The form must set `noValidate`. Otherwise the browser's own email check blocks the contract's messages (AC-004-03, E2E-03).
- The JSON attachment must arrive byte for byte equal to the stored copy (AC-007-02). Send it base64-encoded, so that SMTP does not rewrite line endings.
- Export cells must be string cells with the exact header texts of specification S4.8, `Registered at` and `Consents` among them.
- `server.forward-headers-strategy=native` is needed for AC-008-04 (specification S7.2).

## Measurement exclusions

Decided from `project/02_design/quality-requirements.md` ("Mutation scope"), with no exclusion beyond it. The table was written after the first acceptance tests rather than before them (divergence recorded in `run-log.json`), but it adds nothing to the inputs' defaults.

| Path | Reason |
|---|---|
| `02_output/backend/src/main/java/si/konferenca/registration/RegistrationApplication.java` | Application entry point (`@SpringBootApplication`), no logic |
| `02_output/frontend/src/main.tsx` | Bootstrap file that only mounts the app |
| `02_output/frontend/src/**/*.d.ts` | Type declarations |
| Test files: `src/test/**`, `src/**/*.test.{ts,tsx}`, `src/acceptance/**`, `e2e/**` | Test code never counts |

## Phase 3 run (on the bootstrap skeleton, before any production code)

Run on 2026-10-27 against commits up to `6ec6548`. Logs are in `out/logs/03_backend-acceptance-run.log`, `03_frontend-acceptance-run.log` and `03_e2e-run.log`.

| Suite | Tests | Passed | Failed | Reason for the failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Backend acceptance | 89 | 0 | 89 | Behaviour missing. The skeleton's default Spring Security answers 401 to every `/api` call, so every expected 201, 200 or 400 gets 401. AC-003-03 fails because the skeleton starts with an invalid configuration. No context or startup error, and no harness error. |
| Frontend acceptance | 7 | 0 | 7 | Behaviour missing: there is no `Registration type` radio, so no form is rendered. |
| End-to-end | 5 | 0 | 5 | Behaviour missing. E2E-01..04 time out waiting for the `Registration type` radio. E2E-05 gets 401 instead of 201 when creating its registration. The stack itself was healthy: all four services passed their health checks. |

No test passes on bootstrap code. AC-008-02, which on its own would match the skeleton's default 401, fails at its precondition (registering through the API), and AC-008-04 has its HTTPS control.
